## 7. AI Workflows & Tactics
- Date: 2026-04-19  
  Link: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tDGiWn0flK8  
  Summary: High-view tutorial lays out a practical "agentic workflow" pattern built around Claude Code: define the outcome, let the agent plan steps, have it ask clarifying questions, execute API/tool work, and iteratively self-correct rather than wiring deterministic automations node by node.  
  Why it matters: The core tactic is operationally useful now for small-team automation and internal tooling, even though the source is unverified marketing-style content.

  What it does: Replaces fixed workflow graphs with prompt-driven task execution for variable work such as research, content drafting, support triage, and lightweight engineering tasks.

  Tools/models: Claude Code; optionally external automation stacks and MCP-connected tools as referenced by the creator.

  Setup:
  1. Pick a task with ambiguous steps rather than a fully deterministic process.
  2. Write a goal-based prompt that specifies the outcome, constraints, and success criteria.
  3. Give the agent access only to the tools it actually needs.
  4. Let it propose a plan and ask clarifying questions before execution.
  5. Run the task in short loops, checking outputs and tightening instructions where failure modes appear.
  6. Keep deterministic handoffs for anything compliance-sensitive or production-critical.

  Available now: Yes, as a reproducible workflow pattern; claims about performance gains are not independently verified.

- Date: 2026-04-19  
  Link: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=G0EH0xdy2-E  
  Summary: Creator demonstrates using Claude Code to automate much of a video-editing workflow, implying a pattern where the agent handles repetitive preparation, asset organization, and process coordination around human review points.  
  Why it matters: The useful signal is not "full automation" but partial automation of media pipelines through an agent that can coordinate tools and file operations.

  What it does: Automates pre-edit and post-edit workflow steps while preserving a human approval layer for creative judgments.

  Tools/models: Claude Code; unspecified editing and asset tools.

  Setup:
  1. Break the editing process into ingest, organization, rough-cut support, export prep, and publishing tasks.
  2. Assign only the repetitive tasks to the agent first.
  3. Keep manual checkpoints for edit quality, brand fit, and final approval.
  4. Store templates, naming conventions, and export rules so the agent can reuse them.
  5. Expand automation only after repeated successful runs.

  Available now: Yes in principle; exact implementation details are not fully disclosed in the source.

- Date: 2026-04-19  
  Link: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cJ2QCyr3yzU  
  Summary: High-view personal automation guide frames "Claude Cowork" as a general-purpose agent for email, task handling, and life-admin orchestration; the summary also notes the plugin may no longer work as shown.  
  Why it matters: Tactical takeaway is durable: agent-based personal ops can save time, but brittle integrations are a live risk.

  What it does: Centralizes everyday digital tasks behind an AI assistant that routes work across connected apps.

  Tools/models: Claude Cowork; third-party plugin/integration layer.

  Setup:
  1. Start with low-risk personal admin tasks.
  2. Connect only essential apps and mail/calendar scopes.
  3. Test narrow automations first, such as drafts, reminders, or summarization.
  4. Add approval gates before any send, purchase, or delete action.
  5. Revalidate integrations regularly because plugin behavior can drift or break.

  Available now: Partially; the source itself flags that the plugin may not currently work as demonstrated.

- Date: 2026-04-19  
  Link: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aw_k00T4UFk  
  Summary: Tutorial presents a hybrid workflow pairing Antigravity with Claude Code to build and automate software tasks end to end.  
  Why it matters: The real tactical pattern is tool composition: one agent for coding/execution, another layer for orchestration and automation.

  What it does: Combines code generation/execution with broader workflow automation.

  Tools/models: Antigravity; Claude Code.

  Setup:
  1. Use the orchestration layer to define the broader workflow.
  2. Route code-writing and debugging subtasks to the coding agent.
  3. Keep file, environment, and API permissions tightly scoped.
  4. Validate each stage separately before chaining them.
  5. Log failures so the system can be corrected without re-running the entire flow.

  Available now: Claimed available now, but the source is creator-led and unverified.
